title: Non-blocking follow-up from PR #229 review (backend-trade-journal-followup-review-followups-followups-followups)
description: Non-blocking finding from pr-reviewer's review of PR #229, tracked here so it isn't lost once the PR merges.

checklist.step: PR #229's task-worker amended CLAUDE.md itself (a governance/process document, not application code) unilaterally, via the task's own ordinary task-worker -> pr-reviewer -> pr-decision -> pr-merger pipeline, with no distinct human sign-off gate for governance-document changes specifically. This particular instance was low-risk and appropriate (the parent task's checklist item explicitly asked for this convention to be decided and documented, and the repo has an established, long-running precedent of CLAUDE.md evolving through exactly this same automated pipeline -- see e.g. commits #5, #8, #15, #24, #59, #60, #93, #95, #105, #113 in `git log -- CLAUDE.md`), so this is not a blocking objection to PR #229 itself. But the general question -- whether a change to the project's own governing rulebook (as opposed to ordinary application code or task-board bookkeeping) should require an explicit human touchpoint before merging, rather than being fully agent-authored/agent-reviewed/agent-merged end to end -- has never been explicitly decided and documented anywhere in CLAUDE.md or the agent docs. Worth an explicit decision (e.g. a CLAUDE.md meta-note on whether CLAUDE.md/`.claude/` changes need a human review step, or an explicit statement that the existing pipeline is intentionally sufficient) so the next occurrence doesn't have to re-litigate this from scratch, the same rationale that motivated PR #229's own convention bullet.

questions.question: Should a change to CLAUDE.md or .claude/ (the project's governing rulebook for this autonomous pipeline) require an explicit human touchpoint before merging, separate from the ordinary task-worker -> pr-reviewer -> pr-decision -> pr-merger flow that ordinary code/task-board changes go through end to end without a human in the loop? Or is the existing pipeline (two independent agent passes, since GitHub blocks self-approval and main requires 0 native reviews anyway) intentionally sufficient for governance-document changes too, same as everything else?
questions.context: This is a question about the pipeline's own trust model over the document that defines the pipeline itself -- asking a worker to decide it would be circular (the same pipeline whose authority is in question would be the one settling how much authority it has). PR #229 already made one such edit (adding a house convention bullet) through the ordinary pipeline, and pr-reviewer/pr-decision both judged that specific instance low-risk and let it through, matching a decade of prior CLAUDE.md history evolving the same way -- so this isn't reporting a problem with what already happened, just asking whether to make the policy explicit going forward, and if so what it should say.
